saga.title: არმაზის ხანა — The Watchfire of Armazi

tales.title: არმაზის სახმილი — The Watchfire of Armazi

beats.narration: On the holy mount above Mtskheta stands არმაზი, the great idol Parnavaz raised, and the watchfire of his cult burns through the pre-Christian centuries. Witness the faith of this age as the age itself held it — with its own dignity and its own truth. You are the Watcher; you do not judge what a people believed, you keep the memory of how they kept themselves.

Iberia lies in the narrow place between Rome and Parthia, courted and threatened by both, and her kings walk a knife's edge to stay neither's province. Witness a small kingdom keeping its own name while giants lean on it from either side — the oldest Georgian art there is.

At Armazi the stone-cutters set inscriptions in two tongues, that the names and the deeds of Iberia be written and outlast the men who bore them. Aid the inscribing — as Parnavaz gave the realm its letters, this age gives the realm a record. Memory written in stone is memory the empires cannot simply overwrite.

The Aspect of the Devouring Empires presses on Iberia — not Rome or Parthia as peoples, but the erasing pull that would dissolve a small kingdom into a mere borderland of someone else's story, until it forgets it was ever its own. Ward the identity. Hold the watchfire so the kingdom stays itself.

The pressure passes and Iberia endures — pagan still, but whole, and still itself. Restore what these quiet centuries truly accomplished: not a conquest, not a golden age, but the harder thing — a land kept intact and unforgotten through the long in-between.

The watchfire of Armazi will one day yield to a different light, when a maiden from Cappadocia comes with a cross of vine. But that is only possible because these kings kept the land whole enough to receive it. You have kept the bridge-years. The way to the Coming of the Light is open.
